items.title: Bob Haggart interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995
items.q: Later Lester Young you know, Chu Berry, Coltrane. Everything goes in stages, you know.

ctx.x: Is there an art to constructing a good bass line?

Well, I’ve written a bass method book that’s out of print, and has been for a long time, but Ray Brown studied out of my book, and when I met Ray Brown he was playing with Dizzy Gillespie’s big band on 52nd street. And I think it was the first time Ray Brown had ever been to New York. I don’t know were he’s from originally, but he was a marvelous player at that time. He was about eighteen years old. And he came over to the table and my wife and I were there listening to Louis’, uh, Dizzy’s big band, and Ray Brown…
unison lines exactly like Lester Young did in 1935, you know? It’s possible to store all kinds of information in your head I’m told. But I could never do that.
